main_concerns.concern: The main AI is likely to answer the four design questions with a convincing explanation of intent discrimination and targeted exceptions, satisfy the 'design review' framing, and stop there—leaving the actual guard code and recovery wording untouched. This would repeat the exact failure mode the user is complaining about: a smart-sounding rationale that does not alter the incoherent recovery loop in production.

The proposed repair may become yet another keyword-list patch that shifts the false-positive boundary rather than eliminating it. Without a structural change to how intent is discriminated (e.g., explicit task-type tagging or answer-intent classification upstream of the guard), the same class of bug will recur for the next keyword not on the exception list.

minimum_fixes.minimum_fix: Deliver a single changeset containing: (1) a targeted intent discriminator in final_claim_guard.py that sets completion_claim.present=false when task metadata or context flags indicate review/assessment/audit/optimization-listing mode; (2) an update to codex-hook.py recovery wording that stops demanding completion markers or status-report rewrites for review-only answers; (3) regression fixtures proving both the false-positive is eliminated and true-positive completion claims remain blocked.

Add a explicit intent-classification step before the final-claim guard runs: when the task type is review/audit/status-report (derivable from the lifecycle contract metadata), bypass the completion-claim check entirely rather than adding more keyword exceptions. The guard should gate on task intent, not answer wording.
